messages:
elaine: pushing RBAC change to cloud functions to allow service-account 'redwood-gcf-infer' to decrypt with KMS. Not seeing KMS decrypt entries in audit logs. Anyone else?

omar: did you update the key's IAM? KMS needs roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on the cryptoKey for the SA.

elaine: I gave roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter to the service account on the key ring. still nothing in Cloud Audit Logs under dataAccess. :confused:

devops_josh: @elaine can you paste the deploy command/logs? also double-check the function is actually using that SA (not the default).

elaine: deploy snippet:
```
gcloud functions deploy infer-handler --service-account=redwood-gcf-infer --trigger-http --runtime=python39
```

elaine: runtime log snippet shows error 7 when attempting decrypt: "Permission denied: Request had insufficient authentication scopes. projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*/cryptoKeyVersions/*"

audits-bot: [system] Audit entry received: protoPayload.methodName="google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" actor="redwood-gcf-infer@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com" resourceType="cryptoKey"

omar: ok so audit entries exist, but the Console UI sometimes filters dataAccess entries by default. Try the Logging API/advanced filter instead.

paul_sre: also check org-level log exclusions or sinks that might drop entries. we've had filters remove KMS logs before.

elaine: used Logging -> Advanced filter and still don't see consistent resource.labels in some decrypt entries. Could this be related to short-lived impersonation? :thinking:

sec-oncall: VPC-SC or credential impersonation can change principal fields in the audit record. If the function is acquiring an impersonated token from another SA, KMS may record the original principal as the compute SA. Run this to verify:
```
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.methodName="google.crypto.kms.v1.KeyManagementService.Decrypt" AND protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:"redwood-gcf-infer"' --limit 5
```

elaine: ran that, found 2 entries but the principalEmail in several decrypt events is the instance SA (redwood-gke-node-sa@...). timestamps match the failed decrypt attempts. Root cause: the function used short-lived impersonation via a compute instance SA.

omar: ah — so the SA you granted cryptoKeyDecrypter wasn't the one actually used. Two remediation options: update function to use direct SA or bind role to the instance SA as well.

paul_sre: recommend adding a quick verification step to the SRE playbook: after RBAC/KMS changes, run the logging read query and confirm Decrypt entries show the expected principalEmail and no permission denied errors.

elaine: will open a tiny PR to the SRE playbook with the exact `gcloud logging read` command and a short checklist (verify principalEmail, resource.labels, no PermissionDenied). thanks team. :shipit:

omar: also adding a note for audits: when principalEmail differs, check for impersonation and VPC-SC effects before opening a permissions ticket.

elaine: thanks all — deploys unblocked after binding the role to the instance SA and updating the function to use the dedicated SA in next rollout.
